_doc: AUTHORED reading of Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35 for the district draft's named context buildings off Prairie Avenue (T-2982, piece 1 of T-2162): 213, 215 and 217 East Twentieth Street and 2008 and 2018 Calumet Avenue. The T-1842 census (chicago/prairie_1904_v1/data/sheet_census/sheet-35.json) counts Prairie frontages only and says so ('The Indiana and Calumet frontages of the sheet are not Prairie frontages and are not counted here'; its ruling r35-2018-calumet leaves the Calumet house unplaced), so these five rows are read here, in the same frontage contract, for tools/trace_prairie_1904_footprints.py (sheet '35x') and tools/draft_prairie_1904.py to read. It sits beside the draft rules, not in the Prairie census directory, because tools/sheet_census.py holds that directory to Prairie ranges.

reading.by: Read by eye from the committed sheet 35 scan (1602 x 2000 px) at 3x over the Calumet lots and 4x and 8x over the 20th Street lots, 2026-10-22.
reading.conventions: Sanborn colour: pink brick, blue stone, yellow frame. D = dwelling. Storey figures as printed (B = basement).
reading.limits: A 1911 label is a 1911 observation (study ruling 11): the two Calumet 'GARAGE' buildings are backcast as stables. 213's storey figure is blurred on this scan and reads 3 or 4; the draft takes 3 and says so. No dimension is claimed beyond the trace.

polygons.reading_1911: 3 brick dwelling (D) running nearly the lot's depth, its east wall stepped at the rear (the figure is blurred: 3 or 4)

frontages.why: One of the three rowhouses the study register splits out of pa-213–217-e.-cullerton-street-27 (built c. 1870-1900, standing today); the 1911 sheet draws three separate brick dwellings on the three lots.

polygons.reading_1911: 3 brick dwelling (D) set back behind a front yard closed by a dashed line, a shorter body than its neighbours

frontages.why: The middle house of pa-213–217-e.-cullerton-street-27, which the register says is separately dated; the sheet draws it standing in 1911 and nothing removes it before.

polygons.reading_1911: 3½ brick dwelling (D) with a rounded bay at its street corner, a frame strip across the middle of its plan and a 3-storey rear range with a cut corner

frontages.why: The corner house of pa-213–217-e.-cullerton-street-27, with the copper oriel and turreted gable its photographs show; the sheet's 3½ and corner bay are that house.

polygons.reading_1911: 3B brick dwelling (D) faced in stone (blue) along its Calumet front and its south side, with a canted corner projection and a small frame porch at the south-west
2-storey brick building on the alley lettered GARAGE, with a 1-storey piece at its south end
polygons.note_1904: The Hanford barn: 'P. C. Hanford, two-st'y barn, 2010 Calumet Ave.' (American Architect, 13 September 1884); a garage only by 1911.

frontages.why: Philander C. Hanford house (Jaffray & Scott, 1883; razed 1953): the 1883 permit for 'two-st'y dwell., 2008 Calumet Ave.' and the December 1883 Inland Architect plate; the 1920 sale notice reads '3 story residence ... also 2 sty. brick garage, 75x30', the sheet's two buildings.

polygons.reading_1911: 3B brick dwelling (D) with a 3B rear range, a frame porch on the Calumet front and another on the south side; dashed lines inside the outline
2-storey brick building on the alley lettered GARAGE, with a 1-storey piece at its south end
polygons.note_1904: The Wheeler-Kohn barn: 'To Rent — 2018 Calumet-av., large brick barn, suitable for garage' (Tribune, 24 May 1911).

frontages.why: Calvin T. Wheeler / Joseph A. Kohn house (Otis L. Wheelock, 1870), standing today; not 2018 Prairie (sheet-35.json ruling r35-2018-calumet).
